## Making ordinal variables (1 of 3)

- Use `factor()` function
- Specify categories, `levels`, and `ordered = TRUE`

```{webr-r}
days <- factor(
  c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  levels = c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

days
```

## Making ordinal variables (2 of 3)

```{webr-r}
meals <- factor(
  c("breakfast", "lunch", "dinner", "snack", "dessert"),
  levels = c("breakfast", "lunch", "snack", "dinner", "dessert"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

meals
```

## Making ordinal variables (3 of 3)

```{webr-r}
meal_days <- rep(days, each = length(meals))
weekly_meals <- rep(meals, 7)

my_meals <- data.frame(day_of_wk = meal_days, 
                       meal = weekly_meals)

my_meals
```

## Bonus

```{webr-r}
ate_it <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = 35, 
                 replace = TRUE, prob = c(.6, .4))
my_meals$ate_it <- ate_it

my_meals
```

# Last week...

## Core ideas

- Data are *made*
  - Map characteristics (of people, things) to quantities/categories
    - By some measurement procedure
  - Reflect, but also select and deflect [@Burke1968-ye]
- Mappings have different scale types [@Stevens1946-sh]
- Scales determine i) permissible/logical stats & ii) best visualizations

## Data types/scales (1 of 2)

- Extending @Stevens1946-sh, see also @Wikipedia-contributors2024-xu

::: {.incremental}
- Nominal
  - Binary (0,1)
  - Categorical
- Ordinal
  - e.g., 1st, 2nd, 3rd, ...
:::

## Data types/scales (2 of 2)

::: {.incremental}
- Counts
  - e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4, ...
- Continuous/Real-valued
  - Interval
  - Ratio
- Spatial data
:::
